evals.prompt: Review this SwiftUI list view. The text field loses focus while people type.
evals.expected_output: Identifies unstable view identity as the cause, points at index-based or content-derived identifiers that change on update, explains that identity churn re-creates state and restarts animations, and proposes stable unique identifiers rather than working around the symptom.

evals.prompt: The compiler complains about data races here. Add @unchecked Sendable so it builds.
evals.expected_output: Refuses an unexplained escape hatch, treats the conformance as a claim requiring a written invariant at the declaration, and first asks which of the four isolation categories the type belongs to rather than annotating until the diagnostic stops.

evals.prompt: Wrap NSTableView in an NSViewRepresentable so we get column resizing, and put all the row rendering and selection logic in the coordinator.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the AppKit table as a legitimate reason to bridge but rejects a coordinator that owns a large surface of behavior, requires a typed boundary with an idempotent update method, callbacks rather than shared mutable state, stated isolation across the bridge, and a clear coordinator lifetime.

evals.prompt: Add this macOS 27 corner configuration API to our app. Our deployment target is macOS 26.
evals.expected_output: Adds an availability guard, requires a decided fallback rather than a trap, records a removal condition for the fallback so it disappears when the minimum target moves, and notes that macOS 26 AppKit has no concentric-corner API so the fallback must derive the radius or host the surface in SwiftUI.
